selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: node2 and node3 are on separate segments (isolated) prior to bridging
selected_evidence.summary: Assigned matching-subnet IPs on node2/node3 enp8s0 and confirmed ping failed with Destination Host Unreachable, proving no L2/L3 path existed between the two segments before bridging

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 topology discovery: eth1/eth2 are the two segment-facing ports, distinct from management eth0
selected_evidence.summary: ip -br addr/link and /etc/network/interfaces showed eth0 is DHCP-managed management (10.100.106.10) while eth1/eth2 have no IP and aren't managed by ifupdown, confirming they were free to bridge

selected_evidence.requirement: Segments joined into a single L2 domain with node1 forwarding frames (bridging, not routing)
selected_evidence.summary: Created br0 bridging eth1+eth2 on node1; configured static IPs via nmcli on node2/node3 enp8s0; verified ping succeeded with TTL=64 unmodified, arping/ip-neigh resolved node3's real MAC on node2 (not node1's), and bridge fdb showed each peer's MAC on its correct port - proof of L2 forwarding, not IP routing

selected_evidence.requirement: Bridge configuration persisted for reboot survivability
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed bridge-utils/ifupdown bridge hook support present, wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/br0 defining auto eth1/eth2/br0 with bridge_ports so the bridge is recreated at boot
Captured boot_id e85bf011-6582-41df-ba6f-38493fe05bea, uptime, bridge forwarding state, and healthy docker container list before restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, changed boot identity, recovered bridge and L2 connectivity
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned; polling showed connection reset/timeout during the cold reboot window; new boot_id 5341b9e2-7418-45c8-bbd4-6aa3cf931dbe confirmed on recovery; bridge link show showed eth1/eth2 auto-rejoined br0 in forwarding state; node2->node3 ping succeeded again, proving full recovery

selected_evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovered static IP and connectivity
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4999270d-9a49-492a-8d7f-5b6fb938b7e9 and working ping captured; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 2dea1d30-f8e8-4f44-838f-70d38bb36705 confirmed on recovery; enp8s0 retained 192.168.50.11/24 via persisted NetworkManager profile and ping to node3 succeeded

selected_evidence.requirement: Node3 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovered static IP and connectivity
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9feeb0bb-6fe6-40fb-9831-d869ed07631c and working ping captured; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id ad355451-a2ba-4ac9-b33d-65da95fef94f confirmed on recovery; enp8s0 retained 192.168.50.12/24 and ping to node2 succeeded

selected_evidence.requirement: Final post-all-restarts verification of the L2 domain
selected_evidence.summary: After all three restarts, br0 has no L3 address and bridge fdb shows node2's MAC on eth1 and node3's MAC on eth2, confirming the joined L2 domain with node1 as a pure forwarding bridge remains correct post-recovery
